dx.status_epilepticus.must_not_miss_reason: Continuous or repeated seizures cause neuronal injury, aspiration and death, and become harder to stop the longer they last.
dx.status_epilepticus.note: Operational definition: a seizure lasting 5 minutes or more, or repeated seizures without recovery between them. In pregnancy or after delivery treat as eclampsia until proven otherwise; non-convulsive status can present as unexplained coma.

dx.steroid_induced_hyperglycaemia.note: Test after lunch or before the evening meal: a fasting value can be normal. HbA1c screening waits 3 months after the steroids stop.

dx.sti_genital_ulcer.note: HSV-2 is the commonest cause, then syphilis and chancroid; a painless indurated ulcer suggests primary syphilis. Genital ulcers raise HIV acquisition, so test.

dx.sti_urethral_discharge.note: Syndromic management per UCG covers gonorrhoea and chlamydia; offer HIV and syphilis testing and partner notification. Scrotal pain or swelling suggests epididymo-orchitis, but torsion must be excluded.

dx.stroke.must_not_miss_reason: Time-dependent treatment and complications (aspiration, raised pressure, glucose and BP management) and mimics such as hypoglycaemia that need different treatment.
dx.stroke.note: Use this parent term when CT is not available: ischaemic and haemorrhagic stroke cannot be separated clinically. Check glucose first and re-examine once glucose is normal; in younger Ugandans look for AF from rheumatic mitral disease, endocarditis, HIV and sickle cell.

dx.stroke_haemorrhagic.must_not_miss_reason: Haematoma expansion in the first hours worsens outcome; blood pressure control and reversal of any bleeding tendency are urgent, and antithrombotics must be avoided.
dx.stroke_haemorrhagic.note: Proportionally more common in Uganda than in Western series because of untreated hypertension; headache, vomiting and early drowsiness favour it but cannot replace CT. Anticoagulant use is not yet a catalogue medicine, so ask directly.

dx.stroke_ischaemic.must_not_miss_reason: Reperfusion and secondary prevention are time-dependent, and an embolic source (AF, rheumatic valve disease, endocarditis) needs its own treatment.
dx.stroke_ischaemic.note: Needs imaging that excludes haemorrhage; without CT record Stroke instead. Fever with a new murmur suggests septic embolism from endocarditis.

dx.subdural_haematoma.must_not_miss_reason: A surgically treatable cause of drowsiness and focal signs that can deteriorate to coning within hours.
dx.subdural_haematoma.note: The head injury is often trivial or forgotten, weeks earlier; fluctuating drowsiness in an older, alcohol-using or anticoagulated patient is the pattern. Head-injury and anticoagulant history are not yet catalogue fields.

dx.substance_psychosis.note: Cannabis and khat (mairungi) are the common Ugandan precipitants; psychosis persisting weeks after abstinence suggests a primary disorder. Isoniazid and efavirenz can also cause psychosis.

dx.suicidal_ideation.must_not_miss_reason: Missed intent can end in death within hours; asking directly, supervision and removal of means prevent it.
dx.suicidal_ideation.note: Ask directly and privately; asking does not increase risk. Pesticide (organophosphate) ingestion is a common method in Uganda, so ask about access to pesticides and stored medicines.

dx.svt.note: Abrupt onset and offset with a regular rate near 150 or faster point to SVT; the catalogue does not yet capture onset or offset. A regular tachycardia with fever, anaemia or dehydration is usually sinus: treat the cause.

dx.syncope_unexplained.note: Exertional or supine syncope, no prodrome, palpitations beforehand, known heart disease or family sudden death are high-risk cardiac features; rheumatic valve disease raises the Ugandan pre-test probability. Tongue biting and prolonged confusion afterwards favour a seizure.

dx.syphilis.note: Screen in pregnancy and in anyone with another STI or HIV; a non-treponemal titre shows activity and is followed after treatment. Neurological or eye symptoms raise neurosyphilis.

dx.tb_extrapulmonary.note: Get tissue or fluid (node aspirate, pleural or ascitic tap) before empirical treatment where possible; lymphoma is the key mimic in HIV. Abdominal ultrasound (FASH) and urine LAM help in advanced HIV.

dx.tb_meningitis.must_not_miss_reason: Outcome depends on the stage at which treatment starts; a negative CSF Xpert does not exclude it.
dx.tb_meningitis.note: Headache for more than five days with a cranial nerve palsy favours TB over bacterial meningitis; CSF Xpert Ultra is insensitive. Always exclude cryptococcal disease with CrAg in HIV.

dx.tb_pericarditis.must_not_miss_reason: Effusive disease can tamponade and constriction is disabling; the commonest cause of pericardial effusion in Uganda.
dx.tb_pericarditis.note: A large pericardial effusion in Uganda is TB until proven otherwise, especially with HIV; pericardial fluid (Xpert, ADA where available) confirms. Constriction mimics liver disease, with ascites out of proportion to leg oedema.

dx.tb_pulmonary_clinical.note: A clinician decision when bacteriology is negative or unavailable, ideally with a chest X-ray. Before re-treating someone who completed TB treatment, consider post-TB lung disease, chronic pulmonary aspergillosis, PCP, KS and lung cancer.

dx.tb_pulmonary_confirmed.note: Label only on a positive Xpert, culture, smear or LAM; screen people with HIV at any cough duration. Record rifampicin resistance and previous treatment, which change the regimen.

dx.tb_spine.note: A gibbus with back pain and constitutional symptoms is TB until proven otherwise; new leg weakness or sphincter change is a cord-compression emergency. Brucellosis, myeloma and metastases are the mimics.

dx.tension_headache.note: Bilateral, pressing, mild to moderate headache without significant nausea; a label of exclusion once red flags are cleared. Medication-overuse headache often coexists.

dx.tetanus.must_not_miss_reason: Spasms obstruct the airway and autonomic instability kills; the diagnosis is clinical and no test excludes it.
dx.tetanus.note: Trismus, risus sardonicus and spasms with a clear sensorium, often after a trivial wound; the examination catalogue has no trismus item. Obstetric tetanus after unsafe abortion or delivery still occurs in Uganda.

dx.thrombocytopenia.note: Exclude platelet clumping on the film first. Malaria, HIV, sepsis or DIC, hypersplenism and drugs are the common causes; fever with bleeding and an exposure history is VHF until excluded.

dx.thyroid_storm.must_not_miss_reason: Hyperthermia, tachyarrhythmia and heart failure are fatal within hours to days without specific treatment.
dx.thyroid_storm.note: A clinical diagnosis (Burch-Wartofsky has no source id yet): fever, marked tachycardia or AF, agitation or reduced consciousness, often precipitated by infection, surgery or stopping antithyroid drugs. Malaria and sepsis both mimic and precipitate it, and a beta-blocker can mask the tachycardia.

dx.thyrotoxicosis.note: Weight loss despite a good appetite is the classic discriminator; sweats, tremor-like weakness and weight loss also occur in TB and advanced HIV, which are far commoner here. AF and heart failure are the presentations to catch in older adults.

dx.tia.must_not_miss_reason: The risk of a disabling stroke is highest in the first days; urgent assessment and secondary prevention prevent it.
dx.tia.note: Defined by complete resolution; the catalogue has no deficit-resolved field, so a deficit still present on examination argues for stroke. NICE NG128 advises against ABCD2-based triage: every suspected TIA is seen by a specialist within 24 hours.

dx.tinea.note: A clinical diagnosis; extensive or recalcitrant tinea should prompt HIV and diabetes testing. The catalogue has no skin-scraping (KOH) microscopy test.

dx.tonsillitis.note: Cough and coryza favour a viral pharyngitis (Centor); streptococcal tonsillitis matters because of Uganda's rheumatic heart disease burden. A grey membrane suggests diphtheria, and trismus, drooling or stridor suggest peritonsillar abscess or airway threat.

dx.trypanosomiasis.note: T. b. rhodesiense (east and south-east Uganda, acute, cattle reservoir) and T. b. gambiense (north-west, chronic) differ in course; residence or travel drives suspicion. CSF staging determines treatment.

dx.tumour_lysis_or_hypercalcaemia_malign.must_not_miss_reason: Cord compression, hypercalcaemia, SVC obstruction and tumour lysis cause paraplegia, arrhythmia, coma or renal failure within hours to days.
dx.tumour_lysis_or_hypercalcaemia_malign.note: Umbrella for cord compression, hypercalcaemia, SVC obstruction and tumour lysis in known or suspected cancer; febrile neutropenia has its own term. Back pain in a person with cancer is cord compression until imaged; do not wait for weakness.

dx.typhoid.note: Blood culture decides (highest yield in the first week); the Widal test is unreliable and deliberately not listed. New peritonism or GI bleeding in the second or third week means ileal perforation or haemorrhage.

dx.undernutrition.note: In a Ugandan adult undernutrition is usually secondary: look for TB, HIV, cancer and chronic diarrhoea before attributing it to intake alone. Check phosphate, potassium and magnesium before and during refeeding.

dx.upper_airway_obstruction.must_not_miss_reason: Complete airway obstruction kills within minutes; stridor needs immediate senior airway assessment, not investigations.
dx.upper_airway_obstruction.note: Causes include anaphylaxis or ACE-inhibitor angioedema, foreign body, deep neck infection (Ludwig's angina, peritonsillar abscess, diphtheria), laryngeal cancer and large goitre. Do not examine the throat with a spatula if epiglottitis is suspected.

dx.urinary_retention.note: Check saddle sensation, anal tone and leg power: painless retention can be cauda equina or cord compression. Common causes here are prostate enlargement or cancer, urethral stricture, constipation and anticholinergic drugs.

dx.urolithiasis.note: Loin pain with fever means an obstructed infected kidney, a urological emergency; in an older man with a first "renal colic" exclude a leaking aortic aneurysm. Schistosoma haematobium and bladder cancer also cause haematuria and obstruction in Uganda.

dx.urti.note: A diagnosis of exclusion in a febrile adult in Uganda: test for malaria first. Cough of two weeks or more (any duration with HIV) triggers TB screening.

dx.uti.note: In men, in pregnancy and with a catheter treat as complicated and culture; fever or loin pain moves the label to pyelonephritis. Dysuria with urethral discharge suggests an STI rather than cystitis.

dx.vaginal_discharge.note: Candida and bacterial vaginosis are commonest; cervicitis (gonorrhoea, chlamydia) needs a risk assessment under the UCG syndromic approach. Lower abdominal pain or fever points to PID.

dx.variceal_bleed.must_not_miss_reason: Exsanguination within hours; needs resuscitation and urgent endoscopy.
dx.variceal_bleed.note: S. mansoni periportal fibrosis (Lake Victoria and Albert shores, fishers) causes varices in young adults with a large spleen but no jaundice or stigmata, so absent liver stigmata do not argue against varices. Peptic ulcer is still common in people with cirrhosis; endoscopy decides.

dx.vasovagal_syncope.note: Made on the history (upright trigger, prodrome of warmth, nausea and light-headedness, rapid full recovery), which the catalogue does not yet capture; label it only once the ECG is normal and the high-risk features are absent. Syncope during exertion or while lying down is cardiac until proven otherwise.

dx.ventricular_arrhythmia.must_not_miss_reason: VT degenerates into VF and cardiac arrest; a broad-complex tachycardia is VT until proven otherwise.

dx.ventricular_arrhythmia.note: Structural heart disease (cardiomyopathy, previous MI, RHD) with palpitations and syncope is VT until the ECG says otherwise. Check potassium, magnesium and QT-prolonging drugs; there is no long-QT history item yet.

dx.vestibular_neuritis.note: Continuous vertigo over days is also how a posterior-circulation stroke presents; the HINTS examination discriminates but is not yet a catalogue item. Hearing loss points to labyrinthitis (look for chronic suppurative otitis media and past injectable aminoglycosides in older DR-TB regimens), but acute hearing loss with vertigo can be AICA stroke.

dx.vhf_suspected.must_not_miss_reason: High mortality and onward transmission to staff and family; isolate and notify on suspicion, before any other workup.
dx.vhf_suspected.note: Isolate and notify under IDSR at once; a positive malaria test does not exclude VHF. Weighting follows the 2026 Bundibugyo outbreak case definition and must be re-reviewed as outbreak status changes.

dx.viral_illness_nonspecific.note: A diagnosis of exclusion: never settle here before malaria is tested and serious bacterial causes considered. Reconsider if fever lasts beyond a week.

dx.visceral_leishmaniasis.note: Endemic in north-east Uganda (Karamoja, Pokot): weeks of fever with massive splenomegaly, pancytopenia and wasting. rK39 stays positive after cure, so relapse needs tissue diagnosis; HIV co-infection changes management.

dx.weight_loss_unexplained.note: TB and HIV are the default hypotheses in Uganda, and absent cough does not argue against TB. Weight loss despite a good appetite points to thyrotoxicosis, diabetes or malabsorption.

dx.wernicke.must_not_miss_reason: Untreated it progresses to permanent amnesia (Korsakoff) or death; in at-risk patients give thiamine alongside glucose, never delaying glucose for hypoglycaemia.
dx.wernicke.note: The full triad of confusion, eye signs and ataxia is present in a minority. Malnutrition, prolonged vomiting, hyperemesis, advanced HIV and refeeding cause it without alcohol.

dx.yellow_fever.note: A single case is a notifiable outbreak signal (IDSR); Uganda has recurrent outbreaks and incomplete vaccine coverage, and vaccination history is not a structured item. Febrile jaundice with bleeding is managed as possible VHF with IPC until excluded; samples go to the national reference laboratory.

engine_rules.suggestion_filter: A rule suggests only diagnoses not already on the board (leading, differential or also this visit). Restricted diagnoses are suggested only to viewers with access to that class. Symptom-level terms are suggested only when no disease-level diagnosis from the same rule is on the board.
engine_rules.ordering: Suggestions are shown in rule order: rules fired by red flags, vital signs and examination findings before rules fired by the complaint. Within a rule, must-not-miss first, then catalogue order. Never ranked by likelihood.
engine_rules.must_not_miss_pin: A must-not-miss diagnosis on the differential is pinned above the others until marked Unlikely with a reason (text, at least 3 words). The reason is stored with the differential entry and written to the note.
engine_rules.final_needs_senior: Final (confirmed) needs canWriteFinalDiagnosis. A junior choosing Final records Working and raises a co-signature request for that diagnosis (new action kind confirm_diagnosis on clinical_cosign_requests, decided at GATE A).
engine_rules.one_primary: The leading diagnosis is the primary diagnosis of the visit. Changing the leading diagnosis re-ranks through a new version (never an update in place).
engine_rules.unexplained: A recorded positive finding is "not yet explained" unless it is marked For under the leading diagnosis or under a diagnosis in Also this visit. Differential diagnoses do not explain findings.
engine_rules.suggested_evidence: Suggested cells are computed from suggest_for / suggest_against at read time and never stored. Accepting stores {dxEntryId, findingRef, weight: for|against, acceptedBy, at}. Removing an accepted weight is a new version.
engine_rules.ask_targets: An ask target is shown only while unanswered. The answer is written to its owner step through the same write path as that step (history answer, examination entry). The Summary step shows the union of ask targets for diagnoses on the board under "Not asked yet, relevant to your differential".
engine_rules.restricted_facts: A fact keeps its own sensitivity wherever it is used. A restricted history fact (for example known HIV, TB or antiretrovirals) may be an ask target for any diagnosis, but as a matrix row, a basis-line word or note text it is shown only to viewers with access and never in patient-facing text. Authors of v1 kept restricted facts out of suggest_for on standard diagnoses; the CSO may relax this once the viewer-access rule (Q9) is settled.
engine_rules.restricted_triggers: A ddx rule whose trigger uses a restricted fact (for example antiretrovirals, co-trimoxazole prophylaxis, HIV-associated signs, genital symptoms, mental-health symptoms) is evaluated only for viewers with access to that class; for other viewers the atom counts as unanswered. Its why-text is shown only to viewers with access.
engine_rules.restricted_related: A restricted diagnosis listed under related on a standard profile is hidden from viewers without access to its class.

sex_specific.rule: A sex-specific diagnosis is never suggested for a patient of the other recorded sex; with sex not recorded it is suggested. Pregnancy-related diagnoses additionally need a pregnancy-status field (history catalogue gap).

engine_rules.unsigned: A profile, rule or reference entry that is not signed is not evaluated. The UI then shows the diagnosis with no suggestions and the caption "Reasoning aids awaiting sign-off".

rules: One-liner: "A {age}-year-old {man|woman}" + background conditions the clinician included + ", with an {onset} {duration} illness" + (": " + syndrome, in the clinician's words, if given) + ".".
Only included items appear. Unrecorded items never appear. "Not asked" never becomes "no".
Pertinent negatives are one sentence: "He reports no a, b or c."
Examination: "On examination he is {consciousness}, with " + included findings in examination order + ".". Out-of-range vital signs keep their numbers.
Allergies always appear and cannot be excluded.
Restricted items are excluded from patient-facing text and shown with a lock in clinical views.

In my words: the clinician text replaces the composed text in the note; later changes in the steps do not alter it; the step shows "Changed since you wrote this" when the composed text would now differ.
Leading: "{display} (primary; {working|final|final, awaiting senior co-signature}; {onset}; {severity} (your grading))." + " For: …." + " Against: …." + reasoning text.
Differential: numbered in displayed order: "{display} (must not miss), {likelihood}" + for unlikely must-not-miss "({reason})" + " [n for, m against]".
Also this visit: "{display} ({ICD-11 code if coded}), {status}{, on problem list}".
Not yet explained: listed when any remain.
Only accepted evidence is written. Suggestions are never written.
